comment: Reproducible source list for ir/mch_ir.json (the PRODUCTION artifact). Paths are relative to the mch package dir (indexer/indexer/events/mch/). Order == matcher registration order; equal-priority matchers tie-break on this order. specs_decl/jettons.mch (declarative jetton family) and specs_decl/pton_transfer.mch carry in-spec `priority 90` so they register ahead of the priority-100 specs regardless of position, replacing the former 'a_jettons_decl.mch' filename-sort hack. pton_transfer shares the 0x0f8a7ea5 anchor with jetton_transfer and must stay listed AFTER it: the tie-break on this order is what makes a real (internal-leg) transfer get consumed first, mirroring the legacy matchers list. Regenerate: python -m indexer.events.mch.ir_emit --manifest ton-index-worker/ton-mch-engine/ir/emit_manifest.json -o ton-index-worker/ton-mch-engine/ir/mch_ir.json (run from indexer/ with the venv python). specs_decl/dedust_v2_swap.mch is listed right after the dedust family and BEFORE the stonfi/tonco swap specs, mirroring the legacy matchers list (dedust_v2.matchers() sits between DedustSwapBlockMatcher and StonfiSwapBlockMatcher); it also anchors on btype jetton_transfer, so it must stay after the priority-90 jetton specs that build those blocks. specs/teleitem_auction.mch sits at its file-name-sort position: neither of its anchors (0x487a8e81 / 0x371638ae) is claimed by another spec, so its position carries no tie-break — it happens to mirror the legacy list, where both Teleitem matchers follow the telegram/getgems nft purchase matchers. specs/nft_mint.mch is listed FIRST and carries in-spec `priority 80`: NftMintBlockMatcher is the FIRST entry of event_processing.matchers, ahead of the priority-90 jetton specs, so it claims a deploying leaf before any jetton/DEX matcher can absorb it — and it is what makes `btype nft_mint` available to specs/tonco_liquidity.mch, which binds it. The three coffee files sit in file-name-sort order, which also mirrors the legacy list's deposit -> swap -> withdraw run (coffee_create_vault rides along in coffee_liquidity.mch, one slot earlier than legacy puts it — unobservable, its 0xc0ffee06 anchor is claimed by nothing else). specs/coffee_withdraw.mch anchors on btype jetton_burn, shared with specs/stonfi_v2_withdraw.mch; the two are structurally disjoint so the tie-break is unobservable despite coffee being listed first. specs/nft_sale.mch (the GetGems sale/auction family) sits AFTER specs/getgems.mch and specs/nft_transfer.mch, which is load-bearing twice: its nft_put_on_sale matcher shares the `btype nft_transfer` anchor with getgems_nft_purchase and must lose that tie-break exactly as the legacy list orders them, and four of its matchers BIND nft_transfer / nft_purchase blocks those two specs produce. Matcher order WITHIN the file also matters — nft_finish_auction is listed before nft_cancel_auction because their anchors overlap on the stop/finish opcodes. specs/dedust_v2_claim_fees.mch sits immediately BEFORE specs/dedust_v2_claim_reward.mch, mirroring dedust_v2.matchers() (claim_fees then claim_reward); their anchors (0x5652f1df / 0x909fdb65) are disjoint, so the tie-break is unobservable. specs/tonstakers.mch carries in-spec `priority 85` on all three of its matchers, which IS observable: its withdraw matcher shares the 0x595f07bc JettonBurn anchor with the priority-90 `jetton_burn`, and legacy registers TONStakersWithdrawMatcher ahead of JettonBurnBlockMatcher, so a default priority let the jetton family eat the anchor and suppressed the whole tonstakers withdraw family. specs/dedust_v2_withdraw.mch is listed right after specs_decl/dedust_v2_swap.mch, mirroring dedust_v2.matchers() (swap, failed swap, withdraw); its 0x20b5ef89 anchor and the three inner opcodes are claimed by nothing else, so the tie-break is unobservable — what matters is only that it stays after the priority-90 jetton specs, whose jetton_transfer blocks are its payout legs. specs/elections.mch sits at its file-name-sort position: neither elector anchor (0x4e73744b / 0x47657424) is claimed by another spec and neither matcher binds a block another matcher produces, so it carries no tie-break at all. The three coffee-tail files (specs/coffee_create_pool.mch, specs/coffee_mev.mch, specs/coffee_staking.mch) are listed LAST, in the legacy matchers-list order (create_pool_creator/create_pool 78-79, mev hold funds 80, staking 82-84). That tail position IS load-bearing for the last two: coffee_mev_protect_hold_funds_jetton and coffee_staking_deposit both anchor on `btype jetton_transfer`, shared with ethena_deposit, jvault_stake, stonfi_v1_swap and dedust_v2_swap/failed_swap, and the legacy list registers all of those AHEAD of the coffee tail — so anything but a position behind them would let a coffee matcher steal an anchor legacy gives to another protocol. coffee_staking_deposit has the widest anchor of the three (a BARE btype jetton_transfer, no where-clause) and is therefore dead last. specs/coffee_create_pool.mch carries no tie-break of its own (0xc0ffee23 is claimed by nothing else) but its two matchers are SERIAL — coffee_create_pool anchors on the `coffee_create_pool_creator` btype the matcher above it produces — so their order WITHIN the file is what makes the pair work. specs/dedust_v2_deposit.mch is listed right after specs/dedust_v2_withdraw.mch, completing the dedust_v2.matchers() mirror (swap, failed swap, withdraw, deposit, rejected deposit, partial deposit); its two anchors (0x25251ee0 / 0xdc5ddba1) are claimed by nothing else, so the file's slot carries no tie-break — what matters is only that it stays after the priority-90 jetton specs, whose jetton_transfer blocks are its deposit carriers and its refund legs. Matcher order WITHIN the file IS load-bearing: final and rejected share the 0x25251ee0 anchor (final first, exactly as the reference lists them) and both consume the 0xdc5ddba1 CreditAsset as a parent, so the partial matcher must stay last or it would claim that parent first.
excluded_note: specs/jetton_transfer.mch and specs/jettons.mch are DELIBERATELY OMITTED (A4). They are builder-tier conformance references (duplicate jetton_transfer/burn/mint matchers of specs_decl/jettons.mch), permanently C++-skipped, and inert in Python (decl-jettons at priority 90 consume the blocks first). Keeping them in the production artifact only produced duplicate/ambiguous name-keyed shadow counters + dead SKIP lines. They stay in specs/ for the Python conformance suite (which references them by matcher name), so suffixing was not an option.
